newsitem.title: USA: Phillipine 1997 rates may be single digit - Singson.
newsitem.headline: Phillipine 1997 rates may be single digit - Singson.

text.p: The benchmark interest rate in the Philippines could go down to single digits next year, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Wednesday.

"Going down below ten? I don't think that can happen before the end of December this year," he told Reuters Financial Television. But he agreed it was possible next year as further gains against inflation were made. "We expect inflation to go down some more," he said.

September inflation data for the Philippines is due out in the next few days. "We expect September inflation to be 6 percent or lower," Singson said, noting that would be down from 7.9 percent in August.
The latest 91-day Treasury bill rate of about 11.5 percent was down from almost 13 percent at the start of the year.
Singson thought Phillipine growth would continue. "...I would expect that we should be able to hit the target in the upper range of 7 to 7-1/2 percent (for 1996)," he said.
Growth in 1997 was expected to be in the order of 7 to 8 percent.
Singson also said he expected the Philippine peso to maintain its stability. "So far the exchange rate has been very stable and we expect this to be stable for the rest of year."
